dependencies.$comment: libcurl backs core_http on the ONE platform whose own HTTP stack the engine cannot reach: Linux, which has no system HTTP client. Every other platform drives its own - NSURLSession on Apple, the platform HTTP stack over JNI on Android (core_http/HttpBackendAndroid.cpp), WinHTTP on Windows (core_http/HttpBackendWin.cpp, an OS DLL and no package at all) and the page's fetch on the web - so curl never enters those closures. default-features OFF drops curl's 'non-http' feature (= HTTP_ONLY: no ftp, ldap, smb, ...) and 'ssl' selects OpenSSL over the system CA store, so certificate verification goes through the trust store the platform maintains and the engine never ships a CA bundle.
dependencies.name: curl

render-next.description: Ogre-Next render backend (ORKIGE_RENDER_BACKEND=next - the DEFAULT backend; the default presets macos-debug/macos-release list this feature). Optional so classic-flavor trees (macos-*-classic, ios/android) never build ogre-next; classic ogre stays a base dependency, so a render-next tree carries BOTH backends installed side by side (they are file-disjoint - see ports/ogre-next).
